classification.difficultyReason: Account for the total volume changing with added juice; identify unchanged non-orange fluid as 88% of the final mixture, recover that total, and subtract the initial volume.

content.prompt: Gary makes up a drink so that 10% of the drink is pure orange juice. The remaining 90% of the fluid has no orange juice in it. Gary has 400 mL of the drink in a jug. He wants to add orange juice to the drink so that 12% of the drink is orange juice. How much extra orange juice does he need to add to the jug?

inlines.text: The non-orange fluid stays at 360 mL and becomes 88% of the final drink.

answer.worked:
The non-orange fluid is unchanged when pure orange juice is added.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Non-orange volume}&=\frac{90}{100}\times400\text{ mL}\\\text{Non-orange volume}&=360\text{ mL}\end{align*}$$

In the final drink, the non-orange fluid is $100\%-12\%=88\%$ of the total. Using the unitary method:

$$\begin{align*}\text{Final total volume}&=360\div88\times100\text{ mL}\\\text{Final total volume}&=\frac{4500}{11}\text{ mL}\\\text{Extra orange juice}&=\left(\frac{4500}{11}-400\right)\text{ mL}\\\text{Extra orange juice}&=\frac{100}{11}\text{ mL}\\\text{Extra orange juice}&=9\frac{1}{11}\text{ mL}\end{align*}$$
